headline: Clarity Act advances in Senate, lifting XLM 7% as Bitcoin holds near $78K
summary: Senate Republicans released a final draft of the Clarity Act crypto bill — and Trump's acceptance of ethics provisions gave it real momentum, which Bernstein says is 'definitely not priced in.' Altcoins with regulatory-sensitive narratives led the gains, with Stellar jumping nearly 7% and XRP climbing 4%. Bitcoin rose 1.4% to $77,858, outperforming equities as an AI-sector selloff hit tech stocks. Monero was the day's notable loser, falling 4% as the same regulatory push raised concerns about compliance requirements for privacy-focused assets.

winners.name: Stellar
winners.catalyst: Stellar surged nearly 7% as the Clarity Act crypto bill advanced with Senate Republicans releasing a final draft and Trump accepting ethics provisions, broadly lifting altcoins with regulatory-sensitive narratives. XLM, historically sensitive to payments and regulatory clarity themes, outperformed peers on the positive legislative momentum.

losers.name: Monero
losers.catalyst: Monero fell over 4% as privacy coins faced renewed headwinds amid the broader Clarity Act legislative push, which may impose stricter compliance requirements on anonymity-focused assets. The prior day's Revolut data breach news may have also triggered profit-taking in privacy coins after an initial speculative spike.

whyItMoved:
The day's main driver was legislative: Senate Republicans released what they're calling the final draft of the Clarity Act, a comprehensive crypto regulatory framework, and Trump's agreement to include stricter ethics provisions cleared a significant political obstacle. Bernstein analysts noted the development is 'definitely not priced in,' suggesting markets have not yet fully absorbed the implications of a bill this close to passage.

Altcoins with direct regulatory exposure moved the most. XRP gained 4.1% and Stellar jumped 6.9% — both assets have faced years of legal and regulatory uncertainty, so a credible path to a clear federal framework carries outsized meaning for their holders. Zcash and Hyperliquid also gained roughly 3.8% each, part of a broader altcoin lift. Monero moved in the opposite direction: privacy coins stand to face stricter compliance requirements under any regulatory framework that emphasizes transaction traceability, and Monero fell 4.1% as traders priced in that risk.

Bitcoin's 1.4% gain to $77,858 came with an additional tailwind: an AI-sector selloff hit technology equities, and crypto — Bitcoin in particular — attracted capital that rotated out of tech stocks. BTC dominance ticked upward, consistent with a pattern where Bitcoin draws relative safe-haven flows during equity stress. Ethereum rose 1.2%, broadly in line with Bitcoin rather than leading the altcoin charge.
worthKnowing: The Fed, Bank of England, and Bank of Japan are all scheduled to announce interest-rate decisions this week — a rare convergence of major central bank actions that tends to increase volatility across risk assets.
India announced it is beginning to tokenize its $620 billion corporate bond market, one of the largest sovereign-scale blockchain infrastructure commitments to date.
The UK's Financial Conduct Authority is exploring regulatory exemptions for tokenized gold products, a move that could accelerate real-world asset tokenization in London's financial markets.
